schema:name.description: Name of the laboratory or institution hosting the instrument. Standard cross-TAPP identity field, distinct from the paper-sourced 'Laboratory name' field above.

schema:startDate.description: Date on which the analytical session began. For sessions spanning multiple days, use the date of the first session.

schema:endDate.description: Date on which the analytical session ended. May equal Analysis Start Date for single-day sessions.

anyOf.title: Imaging
anyOf.description: Pre-ablation characterisation imaging (typically cathodoluminescence [CL] or backscattered electron [BSE]) used to reveal internal zoning, inherited cores, and metamict domains for selecting valid spot locations, including the imaging instrument and settings used.

anyOf.title: Ablation Pit Depth/Ablation Rate
anyOf.description: Depth of the ablation pit produced under the registered laser conditions, the method used to measure it, and the resulting per-pulse ablation rate. Characterises the achievable depth/time resolution of the procedure.

anyOf.title: Make-up Gas Flow (L min⁻¹)
anyOf.description: Source and estimated flow rate of any make-up gas added downstream of the ablation cell, including any desolvating nebuliser used for tracer co-aspiration.

anyOf.title: Number of Blocks per Measurement
anyOf.description: Number of measurement blocks acquired per spot. Each block typically begins with a baseline (on-peak zero) measurement before the analytical cycles. Multiple blocks allow inspection of signal stability and within-measurement drift.

anyOf.title: Number of Cycles per Block
anyOf.description: Number of measurement cycles acquired per block. One cycle corresponds to a single set of simultaneous Faraday cup readings integrated for the duration in Integration Time per Cycle.

anyOf.title: Integration Time per Cycle
anyOf.description: Duration of signal integration per measurement cycle. Total integration time per spot = (Number of Cycles per Block) × (Integration Time per Cycle) × (Number of Blocks per Measurement).

anyOf.title: IC Dead Time (ns)
anyOf.description: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in dead-time correction of high count rates.

anyOf.title: Analysis Sequence
anyOf.description: Repeating order of primary calibration standard(s), quality control standard(s), and unknown analyses within a measurement session.

anyOf.title: Number of Replicates
anyOf.description: Number of replicate spot analyses performed on the same grain or nominal location in this session.

anyOf.title: Other Information
anyOf.description: Supplementary methodological context not captured by the structured fields above, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016) — in the source paper's own example, notes on ablation-cell and sample-line configuration for depth-profiling/single-pulse ablation studies, a variant not otherwise in scope for this single-mode (Spot Analysis) TAPP.

anyOf.title: Uncertainty Level and Propagation
anyOf.description: Uncertainty level at which ages/ratios are quoted (e.g., 1σ, 2σ) and the method used to propagate component uncertainties (e.g., quadratic addition) into the final reported value.

anyOf.title: Signal Integration Time
anyOf.description: Actual integration time used for the ablation signal in this analysis. Determined at analysis time by applying the Signal Integration Interval Method to the time-resolved signal.

anyOf.title: Double-Spike Mixing Ratio
anyOf.description: Target proportion of double-spike signal relative to total analyte signal in the spiked mixture. An optimal mixing ratio minimises error propagation through the double-spike inversion. Record 'N/A' if double-spike method is not used.

schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific instrument type classifications. Should include a NeXus base class (e.g. nxs:BaseClass/NXinstrument) and/or technique-specific identifier (e.g. ada:AMSInstrument, GCMD instrument identifier). URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}); free-label strings remain valid. Every instrument additionally carries the Wikidata "measuring instrument" type, which is invariant across techniques: the technique-specific entry says what KIND of instrument this is and varies by profile, while the Wikidata term says that it is an instrument at all, and gives a consumer one term to select on without knowing the ADA vocabulary.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system (a torch, an ICP source, a collision/reaction cell, a spectrometer). A component IS an instrument -- same @type (schema:Product + schema:Thing), same Wikidata term, and its own schema:additionalType token saying which kind of component it is. The shape is restated rather than written as `$ref: '#'`, because resolve_schema replaces a circular ref with an empty stub -- it would read as "a part is an instrument" and enforce nothing. Upstream types a component more loosely (schema:Thing alone, no Wikidata); this narrows it, and the two compose because allOf intersects.

items.description: Distance between the load coil and the sampling cone tip (mm), also called injector depth or torch position. Affects ion transmission efficiency, oxide formation, and doubly-charged species production.

anyOf.title: RF Power (W)
anyOf.description: ICP radiofrequency forward power. Session-tunable within procedure-defined bounds during plasma optimisation; consistent with the analogous, tunable treatment of RF Power across LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS and all three solution ICP-MS TAPPs.

anyOf.title: Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate
anyOf.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma. Determines plasma volume and stability.

anyOf.title: Auxiliary Gas Flow Rate
anyOf.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream that positions the plasma relative to the load coil. Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.

contains.title: RF Power (W)
contains.description: ICP radiofrequency forward power. Session-tunable within procedure-defined bounds during plasma optimisation; consistent with the analogous, tunable treatment of RF Power across LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS and all three solution ICP-MS TAPPs.

contains.description: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma. Determines plasma volume and stability.

contains.title: Auxiliary Gas Flow Rate
contains.description: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream that positions the plasma relative to the load coil. Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.

anyOf.title: Collision Gas Flow Rate
anyOf.description: Flow rate of the collision gas in KED mode. Higher flow rates provide greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity. Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in KED mode.

anyOf.title: Cell Exit Discrimination Voltage
anyOf.description: Kinetic energy discrimination offset voltage applied at the exit of the collision cell in KED mode. Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in KED mode.

anyOf.title: Reaction Gas Flow Rate
anyOf.description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC). Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in DRC mode.

contains.title: Collision Gas Flow Rate
contains.description: Flow rate of the collision gas in KED mode. Higher flow rates provide greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity. Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in KED mode.

contains.title: Cell Exit Discrimination Voltage
contains.description: Kinetic energy discrimination offset voltage applied at the exit of the collision cell in KED mode. Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in KED mode.

contains.title: Reaction Gas Flow Rate
contains.description: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC). Applies to quadrupole-based instruments and to collision-cell-equipped multi-collector instruments (e.g., Nu Sapphire, Thermo Neoma MS/MS) operating in DRC mode.

anyOf.title: Mass Resolution Setting
anyOf.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Fixed at unit resolution for quadrupole instruments; selectable (low/medium/high) for sector-field instruments to balance sensitivity against interference suppression; not applicable in the same sense for multi-collector instruments running static low-resolution collection (see Faraday Cup Array Configuration and Collector Configuration for MC-specific detail).

anyOf.title: ICP Tuning
anyOf.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria.

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
anyOf.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning.

anyOf.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
anyOf.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning.

anyOf.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
anyOf.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses.

contains.title: Mass Resolution Setting
contains.description: Operating mass resolution of the mass analyser. Fixed at unit resolution for quadrupole instruments; selectable (low/medium/high) for sector-field instruments to balance sensitivity against interference suppression; not applicable in the same sense for multi-collector instruments running static low-resolution collection (see Faraday Cup Array Configuration and Collector Configuration for MC-specific detail).

contains.title: ICP Tuning
contains.description: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria.

contains.title: Doubly-Charged Species Monitor
contains.description: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning.

contains.title: Doubly-Charged Species Production
contains.description: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning.

contains.title: Memory Effect Mitigation
contains.description: Procedure applied to identify and minimise memory effects from high-concentration elements in the previous sample or standard that may contaminate subsequent analyses.

ada:laserFluence.description: Laser pulse energy per unit area at the sample surface, the primary control on ablation rate and crater morphology.

allOf.description: Computational tool actually used (acquisition, data reduction, or processing).

schema:name.description: Instrument control and data acquisition software used to collect raw signal data, including version number.
Software used for signal processing, background subtraction, downhole fractionation correction, and age calculation, including version number.

allOf.description: Reference material, calibration standard, or chemical reagent actually used.

@type.description: What the material IS, independent of the role it plays in this run (that is ada:reagentRole). schema:DefinedTerm for a material identified by a registry entry (GeoReM, NIST SRM, USGS); schema:Product for a specific catalogued specimen or purchased lot (Smithsonian NMNH number, IGSN, in-house standard); schema:ChemicalSubstance for a bulk chemical or coating stock.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID). Mirrors tappDefinition $defs/Reagent.

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The registry the schema:termCode belongs to.

schema:name.description: Primary reference material used to calibrate the instrument and convert raw signal intensities to ages/isotope ratios. Include citation for the accepted values used.

ada:spotDiameter.description: Diameter of the laser spot as set in the acquisition method (nominal/target value).

ada:ablationSpotDuration.description: Total on-sample ablation time per spot, as set in the acquisition method.

ada:carrierGasFlowRate.description: Identity and plumbing configuration of the gas used to transport the ablated aerosol from the cell to the torch, including the procedure-registered flow rate(s).

ada:massesMeasured.description: Mass-to-charge positions (isotope masses) this procedure is designed to measure. Defines the scope of the procedure; the analyst may record the specific subset actually measured in a given session.

ada:dwellTimes.description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope, and the settling time allowed between mass jumps, as reported in Table 3 of Horstwood et al. (2016). Applies to sequential (Q/SF) mass-hopping acquisition; for simultaneous multi-collector acquisition see Number of Blocks per Measurement, Number of Cycles per Block, and Integration Time per Cycle.

ada:totalIntegrationTimePerOutputDataPoi.description: Total duty-cycle time for one complete mass-scan sweep (sum of all per-isotope dwell times and settling times), which sets the time resolution of the down-hole signal. Applies to sequential (Q/SF) acquisition.

schema:name.description: Name(s) of the analyst(s) who performed the analysis session. ORCID recommended for persistent identification.

schema:identifier.description: DOI or unique persistent identifier for the registered procedure used in this analysis. Mandatory when submitting analytical data, to encourage formal procedure registration. Enter 'pending' if applied for but not yet minted.

schema:name.description: Other analytical techniques applied to the same sample(s) whose results are intended to be interpreted together with, or used to independently validate, this dataset. Enter 'None' if no coupling is intended.

schema:description.description: Describes (1) the functional relationship between this dataset and the coupled technique, and (2) the analytical sequence — which technique was performed first and why. Required when Coupled Technique(s) is not 'None'.

schema:url.description: Registered procedure DOI for the coupled technique named above.

schema:target.description: DOI or persistent identifier for the co-registered dataset or publication reporting both datasets together.

ada:spotDiameterMeasured.description: Diameter of the laser spot as independently measured on the sample or a test material, distinct from the nominal/target value registered by the procedure.

ada:sensitivityYield.description: Instrument sensitivity expressed as useful yield — the percentage of sampled atoms of a given element that are ultimately detected as ions — for the analytical session, following the method cited.

dqv:value.description: Actual oxide production ratio measured during this analytical session, using the method specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold.

StatisticsCollection.description: Groups one or more Statistics nodes for an instance variable. A typical use is a dataset-level collection holding row-count / mean / stddev Statistics for each measured variable.

@id.description: Identifier for this StatisticsCollection node.

cdi:hasWeight.description: The InstanceVariable whose values were used as weights (inline cdifInstanceVariable node or an @id-reference).

@type.description: Must include both schema:PropertyValue and cdi:InstanceVariable. Additional types may be included.

cdif:physicalDataType.description: identifier or name for the data type concept.

cdif:role.description: Specifies the role this variable plays in a data structure. UnitIdentifier names the unit a row describes; Measure holds observed/derived values; Attribute qualifies an observation; Dimension addresses a cell in a multi-dimensional cube; Descriptor names the variable that a Reference column records values for (long format); ReferenceVariable holds those recorded values.

cdif:simpleUnitOfMeasure.description: The unit in which the data values are measured (kg, pound, euro), expressed as a simple string, in cases where no additional information is available (in the legacy system) or needed (as in the case of broad agreement within the community of use [i.e., ISO country codes, currencies, etc. in SDMX])

cdif:uses.description: Essentially the same as schema:propertyID. References to concepts that this variable measures or represents. When the dataset's distribution carries cdi:isStructuredBy (CDIF Data Structure profile), cdif:uses references the RepresentedVariable that supplies the represented-variable-level properties below, which are then NOT duplicated on the InstanceVariable.

cdi:platformType.description: The application or technical system context in which the variable has been realized - typically a statistical processing package or processing environment (InstanceVariable.platformType).

cdi:source.description: Reference capturing provenance information for this InstanceVariable (InstanceVariable.source).

cdif:isDescribedBy_StatisticsCollection.description: The StatisticsCollection holding summary / category statistics for this InstanceVariable (direct JSON mapping of the DDI-CDI `InstanceVariable.isDescribedBy → StatisticsCollection` association). cdif: namespaced and target-suffixed because the DDI-CDI isDescribedBy association is polymorphic. @id.description: Globally unique, resolvable URI for this concept.

skos:inScheme.description: The concept scheme this concept belongs to. Required for CDIF codelist concepts.

skos:prefLabel.description:
Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string,
a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values.
Each language should appear at most once.

**Uniqueness rule.** Each language should appear at most once in the
set of prefLabel values. Two prefLabel values with duplicate `@language`
tags are non-conformant. Consumers may reject or arbitrarily pick one.

**Relationship to skos:altLabel.** Alternate labels (acronyms,
spelling variants, obsolete names) go on `skos:altLabel`, NOT on
`prefLabel`. A concept has exactly one preferred label per language.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme.

skos:definition.description: Formal definition of this concept. Optional for CDIF codelist concepts. A plain string.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts. If present, each inline concept must also declare skos:broader pointing back to the parent concept. Both skos:narrower and skos:broader must be explicit in CDIF codelists.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts. Required on any concept that appears as a skos:narrower value of another concept. CDIF requires both directions to be explicit for hierarchy traversal.

Each step describes a distinct phase such as sample preparation, instrument calibration, data acquisition, data processing, or quality control. Steps carry their own parameters, instruments, reagents, and may contain sub-steps via schema:actionProcess.

schema:name.description: Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").

schema:description.description: Detailed description of what this step involves.

schema:position.description: Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps).

schema:instrument.description: Instrument or equipment used in this step.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific instrument type classifications. Should include a NeXus base class (e.g. nxs:BaseClass/NXinstrument) and/or technique-specific identifier (e.g. ada:AMSInstrument, GCMD instrument identifier). URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}); free-label strings remain valid. Every instrument additionally carries the Wikidata "measuring instrument" type, which is invariant across techniques: the technique-specific entry says what KIND of instrument this is and varies by profile, while the Wikidata term says that it is an instrument at all, and gives a consumer one term to select on without knowing the ADA vocabulary.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system (a torch, an ICP source, a collision/reaction cell, a spectrometer). A component IS an instrument -- same @type (schema:Product + schema:Thing), same Wikidata term, and its own schema:additionalType token saying which kind of component it is. The shape is restated rather than written as `$ref: '#'`, because resolve_schema replaces a circular ref with an empty stub -- it would read as "a part is an instrument" and enforce nothing. Upstream types a component more loosely (schema:Thing alone, no Wikidata); this narrows it, and the two compose because allOf intersects.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

items.description:
One value of schema:propertyID: a vocabulary URI, a JSON-LD IRI reference, or a DefinedTerm.
Whether the property holding these is an ARRAY depends on which job schema:PropertyValue is doing, because schema.org overloads that one class for several things that ought to be distinct (see the CDIF Core Implementation Guide, "Polymorphism of PropertyValue"):

  * schema:additionalProperty and schema:variableMeasured -- a measured or declared parameter.
    propertyID is 0..* there, so it is ALWAYS an array and a consumer iterates without first
    testing the value's type.
  * schema:identifier -- an identifier for the identifier scheme (DOI, ARK, IGSN). Upstream
    types that one as a bare string or {"@id": ...}, never an array, so do NOT wrap it.

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
schema for a labeled link, a profile of schema.org/CreativeWork
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.

schema:minValue.description: Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in the analyteTemplate.

schema:maxValue.description: Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.

schema:stepValue.description: Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).

schema:valuePattern.description: Regex pattern for validating string values.

schema:multipleValues.description: Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).

ada:fieldScope.description: Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.

ada:category.description: Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.

ada:dataType.description: Expected data type for the parameter value.

schema:unitCode.description: URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.

ada:tier.description: Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.
